title: Wire Python CCP2 CI and fix vector entry points
description:
Scope: Python/vector commands in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/.github/workflows/interop.yml and /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/.github/workflows/ci.yml. Run the actual frozen-corpus consumer and completed Python integration suites, strict schema validation and nonzero collection. Repair the absent python/test/vectors directory command and the no-argument generate.py invocation, since the current generator requires explicit family selection. Reproduce exact commands locally against independent fixtures. Do not bulk-regenerate sibling vectors, weaken legacy gates or modify unrelated CI jobs.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Attach a required CCP2 Python job to existing interop structure. Depend on python.14 and vectors.12, not the .7 rollup or all other language jobs, so independent language verification remains parallel.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow uses existing real test paths and supported scoped generator/check commands. Focused pytest, relevant legacy checks and strict corpus validation run with nonzero case IDs and recorded source/corpus revisions. Missing corpus, unknown case, empty selection, generator failure and a failing production case make the job fail. Existing generator safeguards are reused rather than rebuilt under duplicate jnn2/1lfx issues.
